summary: OBSERVATION OF SILENT MOVEMENT WITH CHANGE OF DIRECTION OF A MASS IN THE SHAPE OF TWO PLATES JOINED WITH FLUORESCENT GREEN ZONES ON THE PERIMETER, RAPID MOVEMENT: lack of information.
description: Recent testimony (March 20, 1975) of an earlier sighting (the witness does not remember the exact date; the case is arbitrarily dated August 1, 1951). In August 1951, around midnight, a witness in Biarritz, at the edge of a cliff, was startled by the passage along the coast of a flying mass shaped like two soup plates placed side by side. Around its perimeter were porthole-shaped areas from which a greenish fluorescence emanated. The trajectory given by the witness was north-south then east-west. The object was seen for 10 to 15 seconds. Frightened, the witness threw himself to the ground, pulling his wife with him, who also saw the mass move. No sound was heard. The witnesses got up, but the object had disappeared. Only one testimony was collected. Certain aspects of the testimony suggest a fireball sighting: the duration of the observation, the impression of proximity, and the greenish fluorescence. However, certain other details do not support this hypothesis (flying mass, change of direction). The lack of a precise date, the single witness account, and the significant delay between the event and the account make this testimony unreliable. GEIPAN classifies this case as Category C due to a lack of essential information and corroboration.

summary: Observations by two pilots in flight of a very bright phenomenon stationary then moving in the sky; pursuit before disappearing over the horizon: strange unidentified phenomenon.
description: On June 15, 1951, at 11:30 a.m., two pilots took off from Orange-Caritat Air Base. One of the pilots was surprised to see a silvery, very bright, circular or spherical object in the sky. He informed his flight leader, who also spotted it. The object was stationary and, according to one of the pilots, located south of the Pelvoux massif (Écrins massif) at the same altitude as the Pelvoux peaks and his aircraft (10,000 feet). The two aircraft pursued the object, which appeared to be growing larger. The object then moved on a slightly ascending trajectory, taking on an oblong shape. The simultaneous observation lasted approximately six minutes before the object disappeared as a dot on the horizon. The investigation conducted at the time by the base commander confirmed the credibility of the sightings. It is noted that some descriptions in these eyewitness accounts suggest a stratospheric balloon observed from a distance. However, the fact that one of the pilots reported the object rapidly moving away when attempting to approach it does not support this hypothesis. GEIPAN classifies this case as D1: unidentified strange phenomenon.
